newsitem.title: UK: UK's CrestCo says no crisis in share settlement.
newsitem.headline: UK's CrestCo says no crisis in share settlement.

text.p: The London stock market's new electronic share settlement system, Crest, is not in crisis and most users are coping with the transition to it quite well, Crestco, the Bank of England-led group developing Crest, said on Thursday. But the CrestCo board is to review the April deadline for full transition to Crest at a board meeting on November 25 after some "teething problems" in the new system.

CrestCo has come under fire in recent days amid press reports that the transition to electronic share settlement has hit severe problems and some London banks' settlement managers believe full transition scheduled for April should be delayed because Crest would not be able to cope.
Last week CrestCo said it was to reschedule the transition of around 10 FTSE 100 securities to create a breathing space to eliminate the backlogs currently being experienced.
CrestCo hopes to rectify over the next couple of weeks what it termed "teething problems" with the Crest software which surfaced after volumes in the system increased.
